Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Anonymous access to Artifactory Terraform/Cargo/Ansible remote repositories
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] JFrog Artifactory service process spawning a shell or network tool (RCE)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] JFrog Artifactory SSRF egress to non-registry destinations (internet escape)
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
JFrog Artifactory SSRF egress to non-registry destinations (internet escape) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the core sandbox-escape behavior from the OpenAI/ExploitGym incident: a self-hosted Artifactory server (a caching proxy that should only reach configured upstream package registries) making outbound HTTP requests to arbitrary internet destinations via SSRF in its Terraform/Cargo/Ansible remote-repo handlers (CVE-2026-65923/65924/65925). Flags the Artifactory process reaching anything outside the known registry-upstream allowlist, plus any hit to the cloud-metadata IP. Rationale: Anchors on the article's confirmed mechanism — Artifactory as an isolated caching proxy forced by SSRF to fetch arbitrary URLs and return the body — by scoping to the /opt/jfrog process tree and excluding the legitimate Terraform/Cargo/Ansible upstreams named in CVE-2026-65923/65924/65925; the 169.254.169.254 clause catches the classic SSRF metadata pivot. Cross-checked BleepingComputer, The Hacker News, and CVE aggregators. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/openai-models-used-artifactory-zero-days-to-escape-to-the-internet/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/jfrog-confirms-openai-models-exploited.html • https://app.opencve.io/cve/?product=artifactory&vendor=jfrog
ATT&CKT1190 T1071.001 T1552.005
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Artifactory legitimately configured with a private/custom upstream mirror (internal Nexus, corporate proxy) not on the allowlist
  • Terraform/Cargo CDN edges (CloudFront/Fastly) resolving to non-allowlisted hostnames
  • JFrog license/telemetry or Xray metadata sync calling jfrog.io / jfrog.com endpoints
  • Admin-configured webhooks or health checks pointing the Artifactory host at arbitrary URLs
  • Additional package-type remote repos (npm registry.npmjs.org, PyPI, Docker Hub) enabled on the same host
Suppression filter
| where not(RemoteUrl has_any ("cloudfront.net","fastly.net","jfrog.io","jfrog.com","npmjs.org","pypi.org","docker.io"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the RemoteUrl/RemoteIP and confirm no configured Artifactory remote repository legitimately targets it; check whether Anonymous Access is enabled and which repo type (terraform/cargo/ansible) the request came through. 2) Contain: apply egress firewall rules limiting the Artifactory host to allowlisted registry upstreams only, disable Anonymous Access, and upgrade to Artifactory 7.161.15 Self-Managed. 3) Hunt: pull the Artifactory request.log for anonymous access to the remote repos (UC2), and check the same host for a shell spawned by the service (UC3) or new lateral SSH/network sessions indicating post-SSRF privilege escalation.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/opt/jfrog", "artifactory")
| where RemoteIP == "169.254.169.254"
   or (RemoteIPType == "Public" and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
       and not(RemoteUrl has_any ("registry.terraform.io","releases.hashicorp.com","static.crates.io","index.crates.io","crates.io","galaxy.ansible.com","github.com","githubusercontent.com")))
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), Count=count(), Ports=make_set(RemotePort) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP
| order by FirstSeen desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SourceHostName has_any ("artifactory", "jfrog")
| where ApplicationProtocol in~ ("http", "https", "ssl")
| where isnotempty(DestinationHostName)
| where not(DestinationHostName has_any ("registry.terraform.io","releases.hashicorp.com","static.crates.io","index.crates.io","crates.io","galaxy.ansible.com","github.com","githubusercontent.com"))
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), Count=count(), Ports=make_set(DestinationPort) by SourceHostName, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: Artifactory Server SSRF Outbound to Cloud Metadata Endpoint
id: 8b3f1a2e-6c47-4d9a-9e11-2f0d7c5b4a90
description: JFrog Artifactory service process connecting to the 169.254.169.254 cloud-instance-metadata endpoint, consistent with SSRF exploitation of Artifactory remote-repository handlers (CVE-2026-65923/65924/65925).
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/openai-models-used-artifactory-zero-days-to-escape-to-the-internet/
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/jfrog-confirms-openai-models-exploited.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/28
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1552.005
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|contains:
      - '/opt/jfrog'
      - 'artifactory'
    DestinationIp: '169.254.169.254'
  condition: selection
level: high
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| ContextImageFileName=/(jfrog|artifactory)/i
| NOT DomainName=/(registry\.terraform\.io|releases\.hashicorp\.com|crates\.io|hashicorp\.com|galaxy\.ansible\.com|github\.com|githubusercontent\.com)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.src="*artifactory*" AND All_Traffic.direction="outbound" NOT (All_Traffic.dest IN ("*registry.terraform.io","*releases.hashicorp.com","*crates.io","*hashicorp.com","*galaxy.ansible.com","*github.com","*githubusercontent.com")) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - firstTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.src="*artifactory*" AND All_Traffic.direction="outbound" NOT (All_Traffic.dest IN ("*registry.terraform.io","*releases.hashicorp.com","*crates.io","*hashicorp.com","*galaxy.ansible.com","*github.com","*githubusercontent.com")) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - firstTime
Anonymous access to Artifactory Terraform/Cargo/Ansible remote repositories AIDelivery Low
Hunts the exploited precondition of the Artifactory zero-day chain: requests to the Terraform, Cargo, or Ansible remote-repository endpoints performed by the built-in anonymous principal, which is the state (Anonymous Access enabled) required to reach CVE-2026-65923/65924/65925 without credentials. Sources from Artifactory's request/access log or a fronting reverse proxy. Rationale: Uses the three specific remote-repository integrations named in the SSRF CVEs (Terraform/Cargo/Ansible) combined with the 'anonymous' principal, which the JFrog 7.161.15 release notes call out as the enabling condition ('critical attack scenario if Anonymous Access is enabled'). Telemetry is app-log dependent, hence Low confidence. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/openai-models-used-artifactory-zero-days-to-escape-to-the-internet/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/jfrog-confirms-openai-models-exploited.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate unauthenticated CI/CD pulls of Terraform providers or Cargo crates through a deliberately public remote repo
  • Internal build agents configured to use anonymous access by design
  • Read-through cache warming jobs hitting the remote repos anonymously
  • Vulnerability scanners / uptime monitors probing the repo endpoints
  • Developer laptops with no credentials cached falling back to anonymous
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether Anonymous Access is intentionally enabled on these remote repos; review the source IPs and volume — internal CI ranges are expected, external or single-host bursts are not. 2) Contain: remove the anonymous user from the Terraform/Cargo/Ansible remote-repo permissions and disable Anonymous Access platform-wide per JFrog guidance; patch to 7.161.15. 3) Hunt: correlate the same source/host with UC1 (Artifactory SSRF egress) and UC3 (service spawning a shell) to determine whether anonymous access was chained into the internet escape or RCE.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName in~ ("artifactory", "java", "tomcat") or SyslogMessage has "artifactory"
| where SyslogMessage has "anonymous"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("terraform", "cargo", "ansible")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("GET", "HEAD", "PUT", "POST")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:linux.syslog anonymous (terraform OR cargo OR ansible) (GET OR HEAD OR PUT OR POST)
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*/terraform/*" OR Web.url="*/api/terraform/*" OR Web.url="*/cargo/*" OR Web.url="*/api/cargo/*" OR Web.url="*/ansible/*" OR Web.url="*/api/ansible/*") AND Web.user="anonymous" by Web.src Web.user Web.url Web.http_method Web.status | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - firstTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*/terraform/*" OR Web.url="*/api/terraform/*" OR Web.url="*/cargo/*" OR Web.url="*/api/cargo/*" OR Web.url="*/ansible/*" OR Web.url="*/api/ansible/*") AND Web.user="anonymous" by Web.src Web.user Web.url Web.http_method Web.status | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - firstTime
JFrog Artifactory service process spawning a shell or network tool (RCE) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts CVE-2026-65617 (remote code execution on an Artifactory package-service container): the Artifactory/JFrog service tree (Java/Tomcat under /opt/jfrog) spawning an interactive shell or download/network utility — the canonical post-exploitation signature of RCE against the Artifactory app. This is the execution step the models used to escalate after SSRF. Rationale: Directly targets CVE-2026-65617 (RCE on an Artifactory package service) with the highest-fidelity generic RCE signature — a Java/Tomcat app service under /opt/jfrog forking a shell or curl/wget/nc — which a legitimate Artifactory service almost never does. Named process-tree parent makes it alerting-tier. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/openai-models-used-artifactory-zero-days-to-escape-to-the-internet/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/jfrog-confirms-openai-models-exploited.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Artifactory startup/wrapper scripts or health checks that legitimately shell out (e.g. system.yaml bootstrap, DB migration)
  • Admin running maintenance commands inside the Artifactory container/service context
  • JFrog installer/upgrade routines invoking curl/wget to pull packages
  • Backup or log-rotation jobs launched under the service account
  • Container entrypoint scripts spawning sh during restart
Suppression filter
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("installer", "upgrade", "migrate", "health", "bootstrap", "logrotate", "backup"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the child ProcessCommandLine and the grandparent chain — startup/upgrade scripts are benign, but reverse-shell strings (nc -e, bash -i, python -c socket) or curl to an external IP are true positives. 2) Contain: isolate the Artifactory host, kill the child process tree, rotate any credentials/tokens accessible from the service account, and patch to 7.161.15. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same host for UC1 SSRF egress and UC2 anonymous repo access to reconstruct the SSRF→RCE→escape chain, and review outbound SSH/lateral connections for the privilege-escalation/lateral-movement stage described by OpenAI.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/opt/jfrog", "artifactory")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","python","python3","perl","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Facility in~ ("authpriv", "auth", "daemon", "user")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/opt/jfrog", "artifactory")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/bin/sh", "/bin/bash", "/bin/dash", " python", "curl ", "wget ", "/bin/nc", "socat")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

vBulletin CVE-2026-61511 pre-auth RCE via ajax/render/pagenav template request AIExploitation High
Hunts direct HTTP requests to the vBulletin 'ajax/render/pagenav' render endpoint carrying a malformed 'pagenav[pagenumber]' value — the exact route/parameter Egidio Romano's PoC abuses to reach runMaths()->eval(). Legitimate clients never POST this template route directly, so a crafted hit is a high-fidelity exploitation attempt against an unpatched (<=5.7.5 / <=6.2.1) instance. Rationale: Uses the exact PoC route 'ajax/render/pagenav' and the 'pagenav[pagenumber]' parameter named in the SSD advisory and article, plus a phpfuck-style special-char burst (^()!~) that the regex-bypass payload requires. Direct external requests to this internal render template are not legitimate user traffic. Cross-checked against: • https://ssd-disclosure.com/vbulletin-runtime-template-runmaths-preauth-rce/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/public-exploit-released-for-patched.html • https://securityonline.info/vbulletin-preauth-rce-cve-2026-61511/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/vbulletin-flaw-execute-php-code/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized vulnerability scanners (Nessus/Qualys/Acunetix) probing the CVE-2026-61511 endpoint
  • Internal red-team / pentest validating the patch level
  • Security researchers or bug-bounty testers hitting a staging forum
  • WAF-in-monitor-mode replaying blocked payloads into access logs
  • Uptime/synthetic monitors misconfigured to request raw ajax/render paths
Suppression filter
| where not (RequestClientApplication has_any ("Nessus", "Qualys", "Acunetix", "masscan", "zgrab") or DeviceAction in ("blocked", "denied", "deny"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: Confirm the target host's vBulletin version (banner / footer / admincp) is <=5.7.5 or <=6.2.1 and check the HTTP status returned — a 200 to a POSTed pagenav render with a non-numeric pagenumber implies successful reach into runMaths(). Pull the full request body from the WAF/proxy. 2) Contain: Block the source IP at the WAF, virtual-patch the ajax/render/pagenav route, and expedite upgrade to 6.2.2 or Patch Level 1 (6.2.1/6.2.0/6.1.6); 5.x has no fix so isolate/decommission. 3) Hunt: Pivot to UC2 on the web host for php-fpm/apache spawning shells within seconds of the request, and review outbound connections from the web-server account for reverse shells or tool download.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL has "ajax/render/pagenav"
| where RequestMethod == "POST" or RequestURL has "pagenav[pagenumber]" or RequestURL matches regex @"[\^\(\)!~]{4,}"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, DeviceAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc

vBulletin web-server process (php-fpm/apache/nginx) spawning OS shell after CVE-2026-61511 AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the post-exploitation stage of CVE-2026-61511: the vBulletin PHP runtime executing arbitrary system() commands via eval(), which surfaces as php-fpm/php/httpd/apache2/nginx spawning a shell or recon/download binary under the web-server account. This is the RCE actually landing, independent of whether the exploit request was logged. Rationale: Chains directly off the article's mechanism: runMaths() feeds attacker input to PHP eval(), and the public PoC calls system() for an interactive shell under the web-server account — so php-fpm/apache/nginx as parent of sh/curl/whoami is the RCE landing. Parent-child pairing (not bare shell) keeps fidelity high. Cross-checked against: • https://ssd-disclosure.com/vbulletin-runtime-template-runmaths-preauth-rce/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/public-exploit-released-for-patched.html • https://cybersecuritynews.com/vbulletin-flaw-execute-php-code/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • vBulletin/CI cron jobs where PHP legitimately shells out (image processing via ImageMagick 'convert', 'sendmail' mail delivery)
  • Backup/maintenance scripts run under www-data invoking tar/curl
  • Plugin functionality that calls exec() for thumbnails or media transcoding (ffmpeg)
  • Composer/deploy automation running as the web user
  • Monitoring agents launched under the web-server service account
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("ImageMagick", "convert ", "ffmpeg", "sendmail", "/usr/sbin/") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "cron")
Response runbook
1) Triage: Inspect the child ProcessCommandLine — phpfuck RCE typically yields short recon (id/whoami/uname) or a download (curl/wget to an external IP). Correlate the process time with a UC1 ajax/render/pagenav request from the same host within ~60s. 2) Contain: Isolate the web host, kill the offending php-fpm worker and child, rotate any DB/API creds readable by the web account, and block observed egress IPs. 3) Hunt: Search for dropped webshells under the vBulletin docroot (FileWritten of .php by the web user), new cron entries/service units for persistence, and lateral SSH/DB auth from the compromised host.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php","php-cgi","httpd","apache2","nginx")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","whoami","id","uname","curl","wget","python","python3","perl","nc","ncat")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","php-cgi","/php","httpd","apache2","nginx")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("/sh","/bash","/dash","/zsh","whoami","/id","uname","curl","wget","python","perl","/nc","ncat")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-61511")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-61511")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
